subject: Re: Staggered completions — p99 increase tied to per-account concurrency caps
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@quantamed.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Quantamed Procurement <procure@quantamed.com>
Date: 2028-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Strange p99 spikes for live checkout — urgent

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing intermittent p99 latency spikes in our production checkout flows this morning around 06:30 UTC. The failures aren't complete errors — many requests stall for 6–12s and then succeed. This has started to affect conversions. Our engineers captured request traces and attached a small bundle (support_logs_QuantaMed_20280605.zip).

Questions:
- Are you seeing anything on your side that would explain staggered completions (lots of requests but long tails)?
- Is there a per-account concurrency limit that could be causing queueing/backpressure?

We have a tight go-live window next week so any short-term mitigation would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Integrations, QuantaMed
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@quantamed.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange p99 spikes for live checkout — urgent

Thanks Ellen — received the logs. We're treating this as high priority. Initial ask: can you confirm the customer-facing workload shape (burstiness, typical tokens/completions per request) and whether the affected traffic is pinned to a single model variant?

Internal plan: Hannah and Monica will do an initial triage of the traces to see if this aligns with queueing/backpressure or a model-side regression. We'll come back with a short mitigation within 90 minutes.

I'll loop in Marissa and Connor for visibility on SLA/renewal risk.

—Rishi
Director, Technical Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-05T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Strange p99 spikes for live checkout — urgent

Quick triage notes from the support bundle:
- Observed many long-tail completions where the server logs show requests queued at per-account worker pools.
- KV cache hit rates look stable; not an immediate cache-eviction problem.
- We do see periodic backpressure originating when the account's concurrency token bucket hits a ceiling — requests are being queued in the runtime for up to ~10s before being scheduled.
- The account is on a reserved-capacity plan but their per-account concurrency cap was set conservatively (20) after a billing tier change earlier this month; their traffic profile peaks at bursts of 60–80 concurrent requests.

Suggested immediate mitigations:
1) Temporarily increase per-account concurrency cap to 80 for QuantaMed to let bursts through while we investigate rate shaping.
2) Apply a short-lived canary routing rule that preferentially places their traffic on a less-saturated pool (low-risk).
3) Enable additional token-bucket telemetry for the next 12h (we can add trace points quickly).

I'll prepare the exact runtime commands and the ops change request. If we do #1 now we should see p99 pull back within a few minutes.

-Hannah
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@quantamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-05T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange p99 spikes for live checkout — urgent

Ellen — thanks for the quick signal and logs. Short update and proposed immediate action:

What we found: early triage shows per-account concurrency caps are creating request queuing during short bursts. This is producing the long-tail completions you see.

Proposed immediate actions (we can implement ASAP, pending your signoff):
- Apply a temporary per-account concurrency increase to 80 for QuantaMed (we'll revert after the peak window).
- Canary route new traffic to a lower-utilization pool for 2 hours.
- We'll stream-side-by-side metrics and give you a one-hour check-in.

We can execute the steps within 15 minutes once you confirm. Attached: cap_change_request_QuantaMed.pdf for audit.

If you prefer, we can also schedule a 20-minute joint runbook call — Hannah and Monica will be on the call.

-Rishi
From: Quantamed Procurement <procure@quantamed.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-05T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange p99 spikes for live checkout — urgent

Rishi / Marissa — we approve the temporary concurrency bump for this weekend's go-live tests. Please note any billing implications and put the change window in the ticket. Procurement also asked that post-mitigation we provide a short architecture note describing longer-term options (smoothing, dynamic caps, or committed throughput).

Thanks,
Kim Reynolds (on behalf of Quantamed Procurement)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-08T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Strange p99 spikes for live checkout — urgent

Final ops note:
- Change executed 2028-06-05T11:28:41-07:00: increased QuantaMed per-account concurrency cap to 80; applied canary routing to pool-us-west-2-lowutil.
- Immediate effect: p99 for the checkout path fell from ~9.8s to ~1.6s in the first 10 minutes; error rate unchanged.
- We kept enhanced telemetry for 48h. No regressions observed.

Next steps (action items):
- Ops to file follow-up JIRA (JIRA-INC-4521) to evaluate dynamic cap strategy vs committed throughput by 2028-06-20.
- PM (Marissa) to coordinate a customer-facing architecture note and commercial options (smoothing, committed throughput).

Attachments: grafana_tailshots_20280608.png (tail-latency before/after snapshot).

-Monica
Technical Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
